title: Everoak Museum — audio guide integration scratch
content:
Context: quick internal capture from call with Everoak Museum (product + ops). They run a distributed set of handheld audio devices and a mobile app. Goal is a hybrid audio guide that augments recorded narration with on-demand clarifications, short summaries, and multilingual Q&A. They want low-latency responses for visitor interactions and robust offline behavior inside the galleries (poor cellular).

Attendees (from call):
- Marta Ruiz (Everoak product)
- Evan Cho (Everoak systems)
- Darren Lee (Everoak audio ops)
- Aisha Patel (Redwood SE)

Primary asks / success criteria:
1) Short answers & summaries from exhibit narratives: 1–2 sentences for clarifications, up to ~150 tokens for micro-essays.
2) Multilingual support (EN, FR, ES) for both transcript ingestion and generation.
3) Offline-first behavior: device should return cached answers immediately if no connectivity; full model fallback when network exists.
4) Privacy: visitor audio not stored long-term; allow ephemeral transcripts (30 days auto-delete) and per-visit opt-out.
5) Cost: target < $0.012 per interaction (ave 120 tokens).

Technical constraints they shared:
- Handheld devices run Android 11, limited RAM, periodic Wi-Fi sync when staff cart passes by.
- Live mobile app can use visitor phone connectivity, but inside galleries connection is spotty.
- Audio is recorded locally, pre-processed to 16 kHz mono and chunked into 15–30s segments.
- They already have transcripts via WhisperX pipeline; accuracy ~88% in noisy rooms.

Initial SE notes (what I pitched / options):
- Option A: Redwood Hosted API + device/local cache. Flow: device sends transcript IDs to Redwood API -> retrieve cached embedding/summary if present -> if not, call hosted generation model -> return and persist both short summary and embedding to per-exhibit cache. Fallback: device serves cached canned responses.
- Option B: Redwood Private (edge VM) placed in museum LAN (on-prem lightweight container). Useful for: low-latency under 100ms, reduced egress/cost, better offline operation. Would require network/VM provisioning on their site and monthly license.
- Option C: Hybrid: local microservice performs prompt templates and exact-match retrieval from small vector DB on-device; heavy generation routed to Hosted/Private when connectivity available.

Gotchas / pain points we identified during call:
- Transcript chunk boundaries cause loss of context; naive chunking leads to repeated answers or incomplete references ("the statue" ambiguity). Need KV cache awareness across segment boundaries for same exhibit session.
- Multilingual detection: visitors sometimes switch languages mid-question. Need reliable language-detection on short utterances; false positives break prompt routing.
- Token inflation from transcripts (stutters/ambient speech) skyrockets costs. Must normalize transcripts aggressively before sending (remove filler tokens, long pauses).
- Embedding dimension mismatch: their existing search stack uses 1024-d vectors (in-house) while our recommended models default to 1536. Need translation layer or reindexing plan.
- Offline consistency: if we allow local device answers from a stale cache, we risk returning outdated exhibit facts (they update content each season). Cache policy needs versioning and low staleness windows (e.g., sync nightly from staff cart).
- Recording consent flows: app must enforce opt-out quickly and we need API flags to not persist or to mark ephemeral.

Preliminary performance targets they mentioned:
- Cold answer latency (full generation): ideally < 800 ms but they can tolerate up to 1500 ms for longer micro-essays.
- Cached answer latency (device or edge): < 150 ms target.
- Throughput: average 1.5 concurrent interactions per gallery during peak; worst-case 12 concurrent when school group arrives.

Immediate PoC proposal (what I sketched live):
Phase 0 — quick lab: 2-week hack to validate UX and core infra
- Ingest 200 pre-recorded exhibit transcripts (3 languages) from Everoak sample bucket.
- Build simple pipeline: WhisperX transcripts -> cleaning (filler removal) -> chunk + session tagging -> generate short summaries with Redwood hosted small generation model -> produce embeddings with an embedding model and store in vector DB (we can use Pinecone/Weaviate for PoC).
- Deliver an Android test app that hits Hosted API and falls back to canned cached responses stored in app (simulated offline).
- Measure: avg token count per interaction, latency (hosted + cold), token cost estimate for projected 10k visits.

Phase 1 — onsite edge/Private evaluation (4–8 weeks):
- Deploy Redwood Private on museum LAN VM; sync overnight catalog updates via secure staff cart.
- Implement device sync protocol + content versioning.
- Test multilingual flow and language detection heuristics.

Rough cost assumptions (very rough, back-of-envelope):
- Hosted: generation model (small) ~ $0.003 / 1k tokens; embedding ~ $0.0006 / vector. With 120 tokens average, ~ $0.00036 per generation + embed cost ~ $0.0006 -> ~ $0.001 per interaction before infra margin; allows hitting their target with batching/caching.
- Private: higher fixed cost (license + infra) but lower per-interaction nominal if on-prem compute amortized over large visitor count.

Action items / next steps (internal):
- Aisha: prepare PoC scope doc + list of sample exhibits to ingest (due 2025-11-10).
- Darren: ask Everoak for 200 sample audio files (raw) and WhisperX transcript dumps, include language labels if possible (requested 2025-11-05).
- Engineering: quick checklist for embedding dimension mismatch options (re-index vs converter shim). Owner: Evan (due 2025-11-12).
- Security/Legal: draft short data retention/consent template for museum use (30-day auto-delete and per-visit opt-out). Owner: Priya (legal) — include in partner PO.

Follow-ups (external):
- Schedule 30-min tech review demo with Marta + Evan w/ Android test app (tentative 2025-11-18).
- Share privacy blurbs and proposed retention settings for their app store review (Marta asked us to send by 2025-11-09).

Notes to self / ideas to test in PoC:
- Test small distillation model that runs on-device (quantized) for single-sentence clarifications — may reduce calls to Hosted API and improve offline UX.
- Experiment with session-aware KV cache in GoldenRetriever-style prompt template to keep exhibit context across segment churn.
- Build automatic transcript cleaner that removes filler words and repeated phrases — observe token reduction and cost delta.

Unresolved questions for customer:
- Are there regulatory requirements around visitor audio in their jurisdictions? (they said they are in EU + US)
- Do staff carts have persistent network or just local storage? What OS/transfer workflow?
- Acceptable SLA for Private deployment? Who maintains hardware on-prem?

End of capture — keep this terse and iterative. Will flesh technical design doc once PoC scope confirmed.
